title: Lord, I Believe a Rest Remains
description: Lord, I Believe a Rest Remains in Tonic Solfa to CAITHNESS, doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Charles Wesley wrote these words. They were printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 228, “There Remaineth a Rest for the People of God”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to CAITHNESS; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Lord, I be-lieve a rest re-mains, To all Thy peo-ple known; A rest where pure en-joy-ment reigns, And Thou art loved a-lone.

lines: Lord, I believe a rest remains,
A rest where pure enjoyment reigns,
A rest, where all our soul's desire
Where fear, and sin, and grief expire,
O, that I now that rest might know,
Now, Father, now the power bestow,
And let me cease from sin.
Remove all hardness from my heart,
To me the rest of faith impart,

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: Charles Wesley died in 1788.
credits: Words by Charles Wesley (1707–1788), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to CAITHNESS by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
